literal: Wei Cao; Mo Han; Liu Kuren
idiomatic: Biographies of Wei Cao, Mo Han, and Liu Kuren

literal: Wei Cao, styled Deyuan, was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Wei Cao, whose style was Deyuan, came from Dai.

literal: In youth he mastered chivalry and possessed talent and stratagem.
idiomatic: As a young man he lived by the code of the knight-errant and showed both talent and strategic mind.

literal: Jin General Who Pacifies the North Wei Guan made Cao a gate officer; he was repeatedly sent to the state and rather attached himself on his own.
idiomatic: Jin's General Who Pacifies the North, Wei Guan, appointed Cao gate officer and often sent him on missions to the Dai state, where Cao gradually built ties of his own.

literal: After the founding ancestor died, together with his nephew Xiong and more than ten clansmen and fellow-townsmen such as Ji Dan, he came in a body to return to the state, urging the Huan and Mu emperors to recruit Jin people; thereafter those of Jin who attached themselves grew somewhat numerous.
idiomatic: When the founding ancestor passed away, Cao came home with his nephew Xiong and a dozen-odd kinsmen and neighbors, among them Ji Dan, and urged the Huan and Mu emperors to welcome Jin subjects. From then on Jin adherents grew steadily in number.

literal: Emperor Huan commended this and made him chief minister, entrusting him with state affairs.
idiomatic: Emperor Huan approved and named him chief minister, charging him with the affairs of the realm.

literal: When the disorders of Liu Yuan and Shi Le arose, he urged Emperor Huan to support and aid the Jin house.
idiomatic: When Liu Yuan and Shi Le threw the north into rebellion, he pressed Emperor Huan to stand with the house of Jin.

literal: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command, hearing of it, approved and memorialized to add military titles.
idiomatic: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command, hearing this, praised the policy and memorialized the throne to grant Cao further military rank.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Right General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.
idiomatic: He rose in stages to Right General and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.

literal: After Emperor Huan died, Cao erected a stele south of Da Hang city, [1] to praise his merit and virtue, saying: "Wei, a scion of Xuanyuan.
idiomatic: After Emperor Huan's death, Cao set up a monument south of Da Hang and [1], to hymn his achievements, began: "The Wei are offspring of the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan.

literal: " It says of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their fame gallops beyond the borders; nine tongues pay them homage.
idiomatic: " Of the Huan and Mu emperors it reads: "Their renown rides beyond the frontier; peoples of nine interpreters bow to them.

literal: Governing the state and ruling the masses, awe and prohibition go forth in full force.
idiomatic: In ruling the realm and commanding the people, their majesty and law ran everywhere.

literal: Their sound stands out among the Hua tribes; they share radiance with pure numen.
idiomatic: Their name shone among the Chinese lineages and matched the light of highest spirit.

literal: Wisdom deep, plans far-reaching, probing the hidden and reaching the utmost bright; in governing, clear judgment; in rise and fall, grasping the heart of things.
idiomatic: Deep in wisdom, far in counsel, they sounded the dark and touched the farthest light; in rule they were lucid and decisive, and in fortune's turns they read the truth of each case.

literal: Benevolence like the spring sun; awesomeness like autumn's frost.
idiomatic: Their grace was the spring sun; their sternness, autumn frost.

literal: The strong did not bully the weak; they hid away care for the orphaned and alone.
idiomatic: The mighty did not crush the meek; they sheltered orphans and the forsaken.

literal: The Way taught benevolent conduct; they transformed without punishments.
idiomatic: The Way they taught was humane action; they changed hearts without the lash.

literal: Within the state no treachery or theft; on the roads, songs of praise.
idiomatic: No traitor or thief walked the land; along the roads people sang their praise.

literal: From west to east, change without form.
idiomatic: From west to east their influence shifted like formless change.

literal: Wherever martial might was aimed, below them no armies crossed.
idiomatic: Where their arms pointed, no foe dared meet them in the field.

literal: South they unified the royal house; north they made the Dingling submit.
idiomatic: To the south they upheld the imperial house; to the north they brought the Dingling to heel.

literal: They summoned and instructed the six Di; all came in returning sincerity.
idiomatic: They called and taught the six Di peoples, and all returned in good faith.

literal: Surpassing what went before and cutting off what came after, they brought this achievement to pass.
idiomatic: Outdoing the past and unmatched thereafter, they brought this triumph into being.

literal: They upheld the Jin emperor and defended the frontier borders.
idiomatic: They served the Jin sovereign and held the marches against invasion.

literal: The royal house had many hardships; heaven's net slackened its cords.
idiomatic: The imperial house knew many calamities; the net of heaven hung loose.

literal: With heroic hearts they aided from afar and did not leave its afflictions.
idiomatic: With heroic hearts they aided from afar and would not abandon Jin in its ruin.

literal: Year by year they cut down rebellious fate; traitors and thieves were wolves and jackals.
idiomatic: Each year they struck down rebellion; traitors and bandits prowled like wolves.

literal: Yong'an year one, the year star at jiazi.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yong'an, the cycle stood at jiazi.

literal: The traitor faction still rebelled; east and west wolves stood at bay.
idiomatic: The rebel clique still defied the throne; east and west, foes crouched like wolves.

literal: They dared press the Son of Heaven; arms and armor rose again and again.
idiomatic: They dared harry the Son of Heaven; war flared up time after time.

literal: Relying on their numbers they indulged in violence and cruelly used the commanders and soldiers.
idiomatic: Trusting their numbers, they rampaged and abused officers and men.

literal: Ye and Luoyang met with rifts; they cast off kin to seek the distant.
idiomatic: Ye and Luoyang split in discord; they forsook their own to court strangers.

literal: Then they recruited violent sorts—the Tuge and the Xiongnu.
idiomatic: Then they called in savage allies: the Tuge and the Xiongnu.

literal: Liu Yuan the traitorous villain banded with them in common cry.
idiomatic: Liu Yuan the renegade joined their faction and shouted with one voice.

literal: They dared strike Bing province and slaughter the guiltless.
idiomatic: They dared strike into Bing and slaughter the innocent.

literal: Ruin and breakage lay like scattered reeds; cities and towns became mounds and ruins.
idiomatic: Devastation spread like trampled fields; towns were heaped into rubble.

literal: Blades crossed for a thousand li; a long serpent blocked the road.
idiomatic: For a thousand li blades crossed; a long serpent of war choked the highways.

literal: Jin's Way answered heaven; its words unfolded good plans.
idiomatic: Jin's mandate answered heaven; its counsel opened sound designs.

literal: Bearer of the staff of office, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing province, Protector of the Xiongnu, Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command—talent and spirit unmatched in the age, strategy and layout surpassing the far horizon.
idiomatic: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command—Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing, Protector of the Xiongnu—was a genius without peer, his designs reaching beyond the horizon.

literal: The times met with many hardships; he feared harm to the imperial sacrifices.
idiomatic: Disaster piled upon disaster; he feared the altars of Jin would fall.

literal: He wished to lead troops forth; the Xianyun burned fierce.
idiomatic: He meant to march out with his host, but the northern Xianyun raged fierce.

literal: He devised expedient measures and plans to aid the hardship with wondrous thought.
idiomatic: He forged expedients and strange counsel to break the siege of calamity.

literal: He wished to summon outside rescue; the court ministers none responded.
idiomatic: He sought aid from beyond the court, but no minister at court would answer.

literal: With high calculation he decided alone and settled the plan of alliance.
idiomatic: Alone he weighed the heights and fixed the plan of alliance.

literal: Thereupon he ordered the foreign state to lead troops within as reserve.
idiomatic: Then he charged the outer state to bring its armies in as a reserve within.

literal: He selected worthy men and chose knights and appointed them envoys of this good mission.
idiomatic: He chose the able and picked knights and named them bearers of this charge.

literal: He sent Staff Officer Hu Lun, gate officer Zhonghang Jia, Marquis of Yiyang Ting Wei Mo, Marquis of Xieyi Ting Wei Jian, and others, galloping with the proclamation document to Jinyang city."
idiomatic: He dispatched Staff Officer Hu Lun, gate officer Zhonghang Jia, Marquis of Yiyang Ting Wei Mo, Marquis of Xieyi Ting Wei Jian, and others to race the imperial summons to Jinyang."

literal: Again it says of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their hearts were at the polar throne.
idiomatic: Again of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their hearts clung to the imperial pole.

literal: The two Weis as chief ministers faced and raised, wing to wing.
idiomatic: The two Wei ministers stood as paired wings to lift the throne.

literal: Cao unfolded literary stratagems; Xiong roused martial valor.
idiomatic: Cao laid out plans in letters; Xiong flamed in deeds of war.

literal: Receiving the command they met in council; in consultation and debate they blazed forth.
idiomatic: Ordered to council, they debated with fire in their speech.

literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi aided and his merit stood out in the Zhou house.
idiomatic: Of old Duke Huan of Qi had aided the throne, and his merit shone in the annals of Zhou.

literal: Illustrious names were loaded on the registers; ranks of reward and full gifts were complete.
idiomatic: His fame filled the records; rewards and gifts were heaped upon him.

literal: The great host turned and moved; splendor gathered like spirits.
idiomatic: The great army wheeled into motion; glory gathered as though spirits had convened.

literal: They raised an army of a million; the term was not to pass a single day.
idiomatic: They mustered a million men, promising victory within a day.

literal: Brothers in one pact, they decided victory in the temple's calculation.
idiomatic: Brothers bound in one oath, they settled victory in the war council of the temple.

literal: Beating drums and clamor they marched south and leveled the perilous and hard."
idiomatic: With drums and battle-cry they marched south and smoothed away danger and hardship."

literal: Again it says: when the two emperors reached their command post, "words like matching tallies.
idiomatic: It adds: when the two emperors took the field, "their words matched like split tally-sticks.

literal: They drew in with intimate good faith; trust and righteousness never shifted.
idiomatic: They received each other in close trust; faith and duty never wavered.

literal: They allied east of the Fen and inscribed the covenant in cinnabar script.
idiomatic: They swore alliance east of the Fen and cut the oath in vermilion on stone.

literal: Forever to uphold and serve; careful at the end as at the first.
idiomatic: To serve forever; to guard the bond at the end as at the beginning.

literal: The covenant charged the generals; elite sharpness led the van.
idiomatic: The sworn pact set the generals marching; picked warriors rode in the van.

literal: South they rescued Nie county; east they relieved Shouyang.
idiomatic: Southward they relieved Nie; eastward they broke the siege of Shouyang.

literal: Straitened towns, darkened, then shone again with light.
idiomatic: Cities that had sunk into darkness burned bright again.

literal: Taiyuan, Xihe, Leping, and Shangdang suddenly met with bandit violence; white bones lay crossed.
idiomatic: Taiyuan, Xihe, Leping, and Shangdang were suddenly ravaged; the dead lay in crossed heaps of bone.

literal: The Jie bandits ran wild; the six commanderies withered in harm.
idiomatic: Jie raiders ran riot; six commanderies were laid waste.

literal: The wicked in throngs answered one another; their plot reached the splendid hall.
idiomatic: Evil men answered one another in crowds; their plot aimed at the throne room itself.

literal: Banners and flags lightly pointed; the Jie faction broke and perished.
idiomatic: At a light signal of banners the Jie hosts shattered and fell.

literal: They sent ten thousand horsemen to advance before them to the Qi and Zhang rivers.
idiomatic: Ten thousand horsemen were sent ahead to the banks of the Qi and Zhang.

literal: Ye then shook apart and collapsed; the vicious rebels ran and fled.
idiomatic: Ye shook apart and collapsed; the traitors fled in rout.

literal: The army held the south of the province; their gleaming blades faced the Taihang.
idiomatic: The army held the southern commanderies; their bright spears pointed at the Taihang.

literal: Wing and guard within and without; they quieted the four quarters.
idiomatic: They shielded the realm within and without and stilled the four quarters.

literal: Their will was to exhaust their strength and uphold and carry the Son of Heaven.
idiomatic: Their will was to spend their last strength upholding the Son of Heaven.

literal: Loyalty and forbearance shone forth; stirred from without, they also repelled.
idiomatic: Loyalty and forbearance lit the age; stirred from without, they drove the foe back as well.

literal: [2] Thereupon they displayed martial might and, shaking the host, turned and returned.
idiomatic: [2] Then they flaunted their arms, rallied the columns, and marched home.

literal: The long road was not of the Yi; going out and entering took a full year.
idiomatic: The road was long and strange; their going and coming spanned a year.

literal: Not a hair was violated; the common people spread their praise.
idiomatic: Not a hair of the people was harmed; folk praised them on every tongue.

literal: They perused the loaded records from antiquity down to the present.
idiomatic: They searched the loaded annals from antiquity to their own day.

literal: They had not heard of an outer domain rushing to rescue an inner affliction.
idiomatic: Never had they read of a border people racing inward to save an imperial crisis.

literal: They abandoned family and grieved for the state, exchanging danger for peace.
idiomatic: They left their homes and grieved for the realm, trading peril for peace.

literal: Only the duke's far-reaching layout—in facing hardship could wield power.
idiomatic: Only the lord's far sight—in hardship he still held authority.

literal: Answering heaven and following the people, grace and virtue long proclaimed.
idiomatic: He answered heaven and followed the people; grace and virtue had long been proclaimed.

literal: He harmonized the Rong and quieted the north; the endangered state was restored."
idiomatic: He made peace with the Rong and stilled the north; the realm in peril lived again."

literal: Again it says of Emperor Huan's governance: "He preserved what was perishing and continued what was cut off.
idiomatic: Again of Emperor Huan's rule: "He preserved the dying line and continued what had been severed.

literal: The wild domains relied on him; the throne endured without ceasing.
idiomatic: The far marches leaned on him; the throne endured unbroken.

literal: Golden tortoise, reed-pipes and drums, light carriages and special regalia.
idiomatic: Golden tortoise insignia, reed-pipes and drums, light carriages and marks of special honor.

literal: Reaching back to the two dynasties, none stood in the same rank.
idiomatic: Looking back through two dynasties, none shared his rank.

literal: The Bing region sighed in praise; the northern states felt his glory.
idiomatic: Bing province sighed in praise; the northern lands felt his glory.

literal: Each exhausted his heart, thinking to raise his fine name.
idiomatic: Each gave his whole heart, eager to lift his noble name.

literal: They carved stone to record merit; images preserved his form.
idiomatic: They carved stone to record his deeds; painted images kept his likeness.

literal: Without ceasing they offered sacrifice; they feasted him with victims.
idiomatic: Sacrifice never ceased; victims were set before him in feast.

literal: Forever handed down to later ages; when gone, no remnant spirit was left.
idiomatic: His fame was handed down forever; in death no shade of him was lost.

literal: Long preserved without decay; extended for a hundred million ages."
idiomatic: He endures undying; his glory stretches through ages beyond counting."

literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Duan Rong of Yanmen, Assistant in Yong province, dug up this stele at Da Hang; though the text is not beautiful, the matter ought to be recorded, and therefore it is copied into the biography.
idiomatic: Early in the Huangxing era, Duan Rong of Yanmen, assistant administrator of Yong province, unearthed this stele at Da Hang. The writing is not elegant, but the events deserve record, and so they are set down here in the biography.

literal: The Huan and Mu emperors both honored Cao with ritual weight.
idiomatic: Both Emperor Huan and Emperor Mu treated Cao with high ceremonial honor.

literal: In Emperor Mu's third year he died.
idiomatic: He died in the third year of Emperor Mu.

literal: At first, among the clansmen and fellow-townsmen who entered the state with Cao: Wei Qin, Marquis of Anle Ting;
idiomatic: Those who had first entered the state with Cao among his kinsmen and neighbors included Wei Qin, Marquis of Anle Ting;

literal: Wei Chong and Wei Qing, both Marquises of Du Ting;
idiomatic: Wei Chong and Wei Qing were both enfeoffed as Marquises of Du Ting;

literal: Wei Ni and Duan Fan, both Generals of Trust and Righteousness and Marquises of Du Ting;
idiomatic: Wei Ni and Duan Fan held the rank of General of Trust and Righteousness and were Marquises of Du Ting;

literal: Wang Fa, General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of Du Ting;
idiomatic: Wang Fa was made General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of Du Ting;
